blocks.x: You've got to sit down and go through it. You know I had a few more things. When you do an interview, you think you've got everything, and you know you don't have everything. Oh, but I wanted you to describe, we talked about a show at the Doudrop. And who were some of the people you worked with at the Doudrop?

Oh, I told you, one of them I can remember. Big Joe Tate on them, White Arnold Harris. Vaughn and Guitru, who were dancers. And a guy called Patsy Veldera. He was a homosexual. And he was the hottest thing at the, because he would come in and dress, dressed up in a dress, and high heel shoes. And sometimes I think he really thought, he believed that he was a woman. He was always the main attraction over there. Whether he was supposed to be the main attraction or nothing. Because he would act just like a woman would act, you know.
Well how popular were the general transvestites and the gay reviews at the Doudrop?
I sometimes wonder if they weren't even more popular than the music.

Oh yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. Now they had a group that, they stopped having, it was a review, they called the Jewel Box Review. They were internationally known. They had about twenty men on that show. And one woman. And the woman would dress up like a man, and the rest of them, all the women would dress up like women. And they would do some beautiful looking men. Oh God. Yeah, they could fool any man, make them think that they were wrong.
Well was the Jewel Box at, was that at the Doudrop?
I don't think they played, they played a lot of theaters. It wasn't from here. Oh, okay.
Well when you had, when you did a show at the Doudrop, did you do a rehearsal, a run-through? Oh yeah, yeah, yeah. At some point? Mm-hmm. Yeah, it was. Was that like in the afternoon or? Yeah.
See at that time when I.
May I have your attention please? Would Jeffrey Barron please come to the circulation desk? Jeffrey Barron please come to the circulation desk. Thank you.
So you'd have some kind of run-through at?
